list.name: server_cpus
list.label: Server CPUs (regex)
list.description: CPUs the Node server is pinned to (taskset)

panels.title: 0. Verdict (PEAK value in the selected time range)
Peak rps
panels.description: Highest achieved requests/s in range.

panels.title: Peak dropped /s
panels.description: Iterations k6 could not start. Above 0 = offered load not delivered.

panels.title: Peak error %
panels.description: k6_http_req_failed_rate.

panels.title: Peak p99 (k6)
panels.description: Client-side p99 from the native histogram (max over range).

panels.title: Peak loop lag p99
panels.description: prom-client idles near 10 ms (timer resolution): warn 20 ms, red 60 ms.

panels.title: Busiest core
panels.description: Highest single-CPU utilisation in range.

panels.title: Peak ListenOverflows/s
panels.description: Accept-queue drops (node_exporter must run in host network mode).

panels.title: Peak FD usage
panels.description: Open fds / limit.

panels.title: 1. Did the test tell the truth? (k6)
Offered vs achieved
panels.description: Healthy = lines overlap. A gap = dropped iterations.

panels.title: Dropped iterations
panels.description: Red bars = k6 could not send on schedule. Latency in that run is not valid.

panels.title: VUs active vs max
panels.description: Active reaching max = responses got slow (Little's Law).

panels.title: Latency percentiles (k6 native histogram, log axis)
panels.description: True per-window percentiles via histogram_quantile(rate()). Dashed line = 50 ms. Needs k6 TREND_AS_NATIVE_HISTOGRAM=true and Prometheus --enable-feature=native-histograms.

panels.title: Error rate
panels.description: Failed request fraction (0-100%). status=0 means no HTTP response.

panels.title: 2. What is the Node process doing? (prom-client)
Event loop lag (log axis)
panels.description: prom-client floor is ~10 ms (timer resolution). Real extra delay = value minus 10 ms.

panels.title: Process CPU (1.0 = one full core)
panels.description: Near 1.0 at the knee proves single-thread saturation.

panels.title: Active handles / requests
panels.description: Open sockets inside Node. Compare with k6 VUs: the rest wait in the kernel.

panels.title: Client p99 vs server p99 / p50
panels.description: Server lines need the custom http_request_duration_seconds histogram. Gap vs client = time queued before Node saw the request.

panels.title: GC time
panels.description: Fraction of time in GC, by kind.

panels.title: Heap / RSS
panels.description: Growth that never returns = leak.

panels.title: File descriptors
panels.description: Open fds vs limit (log axis so both are visible).

panels.title: CPU cost per request (µs)
panels.description: Process CPU seconds / requests served x 1e6, shown above 1000 rps. Kernel (system) share shown separately.

panels.title: Event loop lag excess (minus 10 ms floor)
panels.description: Real queueing delay in the loop, linear axis.

panels.title: 3. Is the machine or kernel the limit? (node_exporter)
Per-CPU utilisation
panels.description: One line per logical CPU. CPUs 0 and 6 are hyperthread siblings of one physical core on your machine.

panels.title: CPU groups: server vs k6 vs spare
panels.description: Edit the CPU regex variables at the top to match your taskset pinning. k6 busiest CPU should stay well below ~70% or the generator is suspect.

panels.title: CPU by mode (whole machine, stacked)
panels.description: Watch softirq (network), iowait, steal.

panels.title: Run queue
panels.description: Running vs logical CPUs. Above the line = CPU contention.

panels.title: Context switches
panels.description: High rates = many runnable threads.

panels.title: TCP retransmits
panels.description: SYN retransmits = dropped connection attempts.

panels.title: Accept queue drops
panels.description: ListenOverflows rising when latency bends = accept queue proof.

panels.title: TCP sockets
panels.description: Dashed = ~28,232 default ephemeral ports.

panels.title: Listen queue length (textfile)
panels.description: Recv-Q = connections waiting for accept(). Send-Q = backlog (511 on your machine). Needs scripts/listen-queue-exporter.sh running.

panels.title: Loopback traffic
panels.description: Bytes through lo.

panels.title: Saturation overlay
panels.description: Left: achieved rps. Right (log): loop lag p99. Red bars: ListenOverflows. Dashed blue: busiest CPU.

panels.title: Run comparison (rps per testid)
panels.description: Overlay runs by selecting several Test IDs.

panels.title: 5. Post-run analysis (collapsed on purpose: expand AFTER the series, with the time range covering all runs)
Per-run summary (offered, achieved, dropped %, latency)
panels.description: One row per testid. Set the time range to cover your whole series, then expand. Red Dropped % = invalid run (latency not trustworthy). Latency = percentile over the whole run. Values are approximate (PromQL increase/extrapolation).

targets.expr: (sum by (testid) (increase(k6_dropped_iterations_total{testid=~"$testid"}[$__range])) or (sum by (testid) (increase(k6_http_reqs_total{testid=~"$testid"}[$__range])) * 0)) / ((sum by (testid) (increase(k6_dropped_iterations_total{testid=~"$testid"}[$__range])) or (sum by (testid) (increase(k6_http_reqs_total{testid=~"$testid"}[$__range])) * 0)) + sum by (testid) (increase(k6_http_reqs_total{testid=~"$testid"}[$__range])))

panels.title: Knee curve: peak achieved rps (X) vs p99 (Y), one dot per run
panels.description: Dots stop moving right and shoot up at the knee. If axes look wrong, edit and choose X = Achieved peak rps, Y = p99.
